name: Child and Dependent Care Tax Credit
who_can_use: To claim the federal Child Tax Credit, you need to meet all of these requirements: You (and your spouse if filing a joint return) have earned income; You paid for care so you could work (you must identify your care provider with their name, address, and tax ID or Social Security Number on your tax return); You're filing as single, head of household, qualifying surviving spouse, or married filing jointly; Who counts as a dependent? A child under age 13 who you claim as a dependent, or; Your spouse or dependent of any age who can't care for themselves due to a physical or mental disability and lives with you for more than half the year; If you qualify for the federal credit, you can also claim the New York State credit when you file your state taxes. The state credit works the same way as the federal credit. You can get an additional NYC credit if you meet all of these requirements: You lived in NYC for all or part of 2025.; You paid childcare expenses for at least one child under age four on December 31, 2025.; Your federal adjusted gross income was $30,000 or less.; You qualified for the New York State credit.
bring: You'll need documents like W-2s, receipts from your care provider, your care provider's tax ID or Social Security Number, and records showing how much you paid for care.
how_to_apply: Online: You must file your federal and New York State tax returns to claim tax credits. If you earned $97,000 or less with qualifying dependents or $68,000 or less without, you can file for free through NYC Free Tax Prep and keep your full refund. For more information, visit nyc.gov/taxprep. https://www.nyc.gov/site/dca/talk-money/file-your-taxes.page | In person: Find your nearest NYC Free Tax Prep site for in-person or drop-off services. https://a866-dcwpwb.nyc.gov/ftps_map/#/?search=%7B%7D
summary_es: Crédito de impuestos que le devuelve dinero si pagó cuidado de niños o de un dependiente con discapacidad para poder trabajar o buscar trabajo.
summary_en: Tax credit that gives money back if you paid for child care or care of a disabled dependent so you could work or look for work.

name: Child Tax Credit (CTC)
who_can_use: To claim the federal Child Tax Credit, you need to meet all of these requirements: Filing status Annual income limit Single, head of household, or qualifying surviving spouse Up to $200,000 Married filing jointly Up to $400,000 You must have: A child, stepchild, grandchild, foster child, adopted child, sibling, niece, or nephew under age 17; A Social Security Number (SSN) or Adoption Tax Identification Number (ATIN) for yourself and your dependent(s); Lived with your dependent(s) for more than half the year in the US; Claimed the dependent on your tax return (the dependent cannot provide more than half of their own financial support) ; Important: Only one parent can claim a child for the CTC. If you share custody, talk with the other parent about who will claim your child to avoid filing issues. Requirements for the Empire State Child Tax Credit You qualify if you're a full-year New York State resident or are married to one, have a qualifying child, and meet one of these requirements: You claimed the federal CTC, or; Your New York adjusted gross income is $75,000 or less (single/head of household), $110,000 or less (married filing jointly), or $55,000 or less (married filing separately); Each child listed on your claim needs a valid SSN or Individual Taxpayer Identification Number (ITIN).
status_note: Requires an SSN or ATIN for you and your dependents; each child listed on the claim needs a valid SSN or ITIN. If you have questions about how this applies to you, talk with a free legal provider before applying.

name: Senior Citizen Homeowners' Exemption (SCHE)
who_can_use: To be eligible for SCHE, you must meet these requirements: Own a one-, two-, or three-family home, condo, or coop apartment.; All owners of the property are 65 or older. However, if you own the property with a spouse or sibling, only one of you need to be 65 or older.; All owners must live on the property as the primary residence.; The combined income for all owners must be less than or equal to $58,399.; You must own the property for at least 12 consecutive months before the date of filing for the exemption. This is not a requirement if you got the exemption on a property that you owned before.
bring: To apply for SCHE you will need to prove the following: Your age: you need a copy of a government-issued ID; Your income: copies of federal tax returns and additional forms (schedules) for all owners. If any owners do not file a tax return, provide proof of yearly earnings.; Your deductions:Copies of receipts for your paid medical bills not covered by insurance for your income documentation year, OR; Copy of your Schedule A; Depending on your application, you may need a trust agreement, will, or other legal documents.
how_to_apply: Apply by March 15 for benefits to begin on July 1 of the same year. If March 15 falls on a weekend or holiday, the deadline is the next business day. bring: View the pre-registration checklist to learn more about the documents you need to pre-register your child and accept their 3-K offer.
how_to_apply: Apply for 3-K in one of these ways: Online with MySchools. name: Accelerated Study in Associate Programs (CUNY ASAP)
who_can_use: To be eligible for CUNY ASAP, you should: Apply and be accepted to a CUNY college that offers ASAP; Be a New York City resident or eligible for in-state tuition; Agree to enter into a full-time associate degree program in an ASAP-approved major; Be proficient in Math and/or English (reading and writing) ; Have no more than 15 college credits and a minimum GPA of 2.0.
how_to_apply: To join ASAP, follow these easy steps: Apply to a CUNY college that has ASAP.; Complete the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) and the New York State Tuition Assistance Program (TAP) application. Students under the New York State Dream Act may be eligible to receive state aid, including TAP, Excelsior, and other state-run scholarships.; Accept your offer of admission.; Complete all admissions requirements for your college.; Check your college's ASAP website for information on additional needs and next steps.; Note: To join ASAP, students must complete the FAFSA and New York State TAP application each year and accept any federal and state grant aid awarded (Pell, SEOG, TAP). Students under the New York State Dream Act may be eligible to receive state aid, including TAP, Excelsior, and other state-run scholarships. If you are or were in foster care, you can receive additional benefits, such as: Tuition and fee gap scholarship (Admissions, CUNY Start, and Math Start); Intersession tuition assistance (Free summer and winter courses); Full coverage of MetroCards (Replacement MetroCards); Full coverage of all textbooks and more; Students between the ages of 17-25, currently or formerly in foster care, and enrolled or on track to join ASAP or ACE are encouraged to register for the CUNY ASAP Foster Care Initiative. | Online: To join ASAP, follow these easy steps: Apply to a CUNY college that has ASAP.; Complete the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) and the New York State Tuition Assistance Program (TAP) application.; Accept your offer of admission.; Complete all admissions requirements for your college.; Check your college's ASAP website for information on additional needs and next steps.; Note: To join ASAP, students must complete the FAFSA and New York State TAP application each year and accept any federal and state grant aid awarded (Pell, SEOG, TAP). Students under the New York State Dream Act may be eligible to receive state aid, including TAP, Excelsior, and other state-run scholarships. http://www2.cuny.edu/admissions/
summary_es: Apoyo económico, académico y personal para que estudiantes de CUNY terminen su título asociado.
summary_en: Financial, academic, and personal support to help CUNY students finish an associate degree.

summary_es: Ayuda a estudiantes de CUNY a cumplir los estándares de competencia y prepararse para cursos universitarios.
summary_en: Helps CUNY students meet proficiency standards and prepare for college-level courses.

how_to_apply: Find a program on the DiscoverDYCD website by typing "Train & Earn" into the "Program Search" box. summary_es: Capacitación laboral, ayuda para conseguir empleo y preparación para el examen de equivalencia de secundaria para jóvenes que no trabajan ni estudian.
summary_en: Job training, employment help, and high school equivalency test prep for young people who are not working or in school.

name: NYC Ladders for Leaders
who_can_use: You may be eligible if you can answer yes to these questions. bring: You do not need to submit documents with your application. You will only need to submit documents if you are selected to participate in the program. You will need to provide the following unexpired documents: Proof of who you are One of the following: School ID; City, state, or government-issued ID, such as a NYS driver license, learner's permit, passport, or IDNYC; Proof of your age One of the following: Birth certificate ; Benefit card ; NYS Driver license/learner's permit; Non-citizen (alien) registration card ; U.S. Passport; Proof of where you live One of the following, dated in the last 6 months: Home utility bill ; Lease, mortgage, or deed ; Cable bill (must have phone service listed) ; Official mail from a Federal, State or City Agency; Proof of work eligibility Youth 16 and 17 years old will need to provide their working papers. In addition, all youth will need to provide one of the following: Report card (dated within the last 6 months ) ; Official school transcript ; NYS Driver license/learner's permit; Voters registration card ; U.S. military card/draft record ; Proof of school status One of the following: Official high school transcript ; Official college transcript ; Unofficial college transcript with a copy of your college ID; Proof of citizenship status One of the following: Valid U.S. Passport ; U.S. Birth Certificate ; Alien registration card ; I-94, I-551, I-797 ; Certificate of naturalization ; Employment registration card; Proof of your family's income For each income source of each income earner and dated in the last 6 months, any one document: If supported by Public Assistance: Current EBT Card (with parent/guardian name) AND a recent store receipt ; Current Benefit Budget/SNAP Letter ; Official letter from Social Services (Must include applicants name, Benefit #, and date) ; If not supported by Public Assistance: Two (2) consecutive pay stubs dated within the last six months (Must include payee name, and gross income) ; 2021 W-2 form and one (1) pay stub dated within the last six months; Current Pension Award letter ; Current SSA Award letter ; Unemployment Benefit Document dated within the last six months ; If self-employed, 2021 Tax Return including Schedule C or E (if receiving rental income); Proof of social security number Social Security Card; Proof of Selective Service registration (for males 18 and older) One of the following: Record of online registration (www.sss.gov); Online receipt ; Proof of disability status (if applicable) One of the following: Proof of Social Security Disability or Supplemental Security Income (SSI); Statement from medical professional; Other official documentation for ACS, HRA, your school stating you have a disability
how_to_apply: Apply to Ladders for Leaders in late January / early February.; The application for Ladders for Leaders is only available during the application period. | Online: Apply to Ladders for Leaders in late January / early February.; The application for Ladders for Leaders is only available during the application period. https://application.nycsyep.com/
summary_es: Pasantías pagadas de verano en empresas, organizaciones sin fines de lucro y agencias de NYC para estudiantes de secundaria y universidad.

how_to_apply: Online: Apply at NY State of Health if you are: Under 65; Pregnant; A child; Apply at ACCESS HRA if you are: 65 or older; On Medicare with no minor children; Living with a disability or blindness; Under 26 and previously in foster care | In person: Visit any Medicaid office or a health insurance assistor to enroll in-person for free. | By phone: For adults under 65, pregnant women, and children: Call 855-355-5777 or TTY: 800-662-1220; If you're in one of the groups below, call 347-396-4705, a Facilitated Enroller, or HRA at 888-692-6116:adults 65 or older; receiving Medicare and are not a parent/caretaker relative of minor children,; living with a disability and/or blindness; a young adult under age 26 who was under foster care in the past; If you're an undocumented immigrant 65 or older, call HRA at 347-396-4705 to enroll.
summary_es: Cobertura médica para visitas al médico y clínica, chequeos, vacunas y más para residentes de Nueva York que cumplen límites de ingresos. Inscripción todo el año.
summary_en: Health coverage for doctor and clinic visits, checkups, immunizations, and more for New York residents who meet income limits. Enroll any time.

name: Big Apple Connect
who_can_use: You can enroll in Big Apple Connect if you live in any of these NYCHA developments .
how_to_apply: Call your cable provider (Optimum or Spectrum). Optimum: 866-580-1410; Spectrum: 866-960-1754 | By phone: Call your cable provider (Optimum or Spectrum). Optimum: 866-580-1410; Spectrum: 866-960-1754
summary_es: Internet en casa y cable básico desde $0 al mes para residentes de desarrollos participantes de NYCHA, con Optimum o Spectrum.
summary_en: Home internet and basic cable for as low as $0 a month for residents of participating NYCHA developments, through Optimum or Spectrum.

status_note: Must be a New York State resident and meet immigration status requirements. If you have questions about how this applies to you, talk with a free legal provider before applying.
bring: You'll need the following for each member of your household: Birth dates; Social security numbers; Employment, income, and health insurance information
how_to_apply: Enroll any time of year in one of the following ways: Visit the NY State of Health; Call 855-355-5777 or 311.; Find an in-person enroller near you. | Online: Enroll at the NY State of Health. http://www.nystateofhealth.ny.gov/ | In person: Find an in-person enrollment assistor near you. | By phone: Call 855-355-5777 or 311 to ask about applying to Essential Plan.
summary_es: Seguro médico sin prima mensual y con bajos costos para residentes de Nueva York de 19 a 64 años. Inscripción todo el año.
summary_en: Health insurance with $0 monthly premiums and low costs for New York residents ages 19 to 64. Enroll any time of year.

name: NYC Ferry Discount Program
who_can_use: Get discounted one-way ferry tickets if you're: 65 or older; A person with a disability; A NYC high school student; A Fair Fares NYC participant
status_note: Open to all New Yorkers regardless of immigration status (NYC Benefits dataset tag).
how_to_apply: For seniors, people with disabilities, and Fair Fares NYC participants: Visit the NYC Ferry website to fill out the Ferry Discount Application form and submit all required documents. You can also print and mail an application form: Persons with disabilities; Senior citizens, aged 65 and older; Current participants in the Fair Fares NYC program; Processing time may take up to 30 days. For high school students: Log into or create a NYC Student Account (NYCSA).Parents/guardians of NYC nonpublic and charter high school students can create a NYCSA. summary_es: Tarifas reducidas de NYC Ferry para mayores de 65 años, personas con discapacidad, estudiantes de secundaria y participantes de Fair Fares NYC.
summary_en: Discounted NYC Ferry fares for seniors 65+, people with disabilities, high school students, and Fair Fares NYC participants.

name: MTA Reduced-Fare Program
who_can_use: You qualify if any of the following apply: Are 65 or older; Receive Medicare benefits for any reason other than age; Have a serious mental illness and receive Supplemental Security Income (SSI); Have blindness; Have deafness or hearing loss; Have an ambulatory, cognitive, or other physical disability
bring: Use any one of these to apply: Driver's license from any state; Passport from any country; IDNYC; Birth certificate (with a photo ID); Medicare card (with a photo ID)
how_to_apply: In person: Apply in person at: Customer Service Centers at select accessible subway stations, open 24/7; The Customer Service Center at 3 Stone St in Lower Manhattan on weekdays, 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. (except major holidays); Mobile Sales vehicles in your neighborhood; If you're 65 or older: Sign up in person and get your new Reduced-Fare OMNY card the same day. If you have a disability: Get in-person, individualized assistance. It may take longer to receive your card if your application needs extra review. | By mail: Download and complete an applicationFor people 65 and older; For people with disabilities; Include a passport-style photo; Include a copy of a valid ID as proof of age; For riders with disabilities, include documentation of a qualifying disability; Mail your application and documents to: MTA New York City Transit Attn: Reduced Fare Program 130 Livingston St Brooklyn, NY 11201-9625
summary_es: Tarifas reducidas del MTA para personas de 65 años o más o con una discapacidad que califica.
summary_en: Reduced MTA fares for anyone 65 or older or with a qualifying disability.

name: NYS Paid Prenatal Leave
who_can_use: See if you're eligible for Paid Prenatal Leave: Eligible employees Full- and part-time employees in the private sector; Employees of non-profit organizations; Not eligible Federal, state, or local government employees
how_to_apply: In person: Tell your employer if you plan on taking Paid Prenatal Leave, just like you would do for other kinds of leave. Your employer must let you take Paid Prenatal Leave when you ask.
summary_es: Por ley del estado de Nueva York, los trabajadores tienen 20 horas de licencia prenatal pagada cada año.
summary_en: By New York State law, workers get 20 hours of paid prenatal leave every year.

name: Affordable Broadband Act (ABA)
who_can_use: You may qualify for low-cost home internet if someone in your household receives any of the following benefits: Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program; Medicaid; Senior Citizen Rent Increase Exemption; Disability Rent Increase Exemption ; Affordability benefit from a utility, such as the Home Energy Assistance Program (HEAP); Free or reduced-priced lunch through the National School Lunch Program; Not enrolled in any qualifying programs? You may still qualify based on household income. Contact your internet provider for income limits.
how_to_apply: Online: Find an internet service provider (ISP) that serves your address. Look for terms like "low cost," "reduced cost," or "Affordable Broadband Act" on provider websites. Popular programs include Spectrum Internet Assist, Optimum Advantage, and Verizon Forward. Verify your eligibility directly through the ISP to apply. https://mapmybroadband.dps.ny.gov/
summary_es: Internet en casa con descuento si recibe SNAP, Medicaid u otros beneficios.
summary_en: Discounted home internet if you receive SNAP, Medicaid, or other benefits.

name: Summer EBT
who_can_use: Most eligible kids between ages 6 to 16 are approved automatically. You do not need to apply if your child is enrolled in: SNAP (food stamps); Cash assistance; Medicaid; Free or reduced-price school meals; If you qualify automatically, youll get a letter in the mail. Not automatically approved? You can apply if both of the following are true: Your child attends a school in the National School Lunch Program (NSLP); Your household income is at or below the monthly limits; Household size Maximum monthly income for 2026 1 $2,461 2 $3,337 3 $4,212 4 $5,088 5 $5,964 6 $6,839 7 $7,715 8 $8,591 Each additional person +$876
how_to_apply: Online: Most eligible households do not need to apply. If you think you qualify and have not received a notice in the mail by June 16, apply online before September 8, 2026. https://summerebt.ny.gov/en-US/Before-You-Begin/
summary_es: Niños elegibles de 6 a 16 años reciben $120 para comprar comida cuando no hay clases en el verano.
summary_en: Eligible kids ages 6 to 16 get $120 for groceries when school is out for the summer.

name: Senator José Peralta NYS DREAM Act
who_can_use: Students who received their high school degree or GED in New York State and students receiving in-state tuition, including undocumented students. Accepted statuses: T visa holder; U visa holder; Temporary Protected Status (TPS); DACA recipient; pending lawful immigration status; U.S. citizens and permanent residents whose permanent home is outside NYS. Educational requirements: graduated from a NYS high school after attending for at least two years; or received a NYS high school equivalency diploma; or were charged in-state tuition at a SUNY or CUNY campus for reasons other than residency.
status_note: Open to undocumented students, DACA recipients, TPS, T visa and U visa holders, and people with pending lawful status. Applicants without lawful immigration status will not be asked for their home address and will not have to upload financial records. If you have questions about how this applies to you, talk with a free legal provider before applying.
bring: Applicants without lawful immigration status are not asked for a home address and do not upload financial records. Any required documents are uploaded through the NYS DREAM Act portal.
how_to_apply: Apply for NYS DREAM Act eligibility online at https://nysdream.applyists.net/ (open year-round; apply only once). After approval, apply for TAP and other NYS awards through the same portal each year. Help: HESC support sessions (www.hesc.ny.gov/get-help/find-event) or the help chat in your HESC ISTS student account.
summary_es: Estudiantes indocumentados y otros que terminaron la secundaria o el GED en Nueva York pueden recibir ayuda estatal para la universidad, como TAP y Excelsior. Se solicita una vez.
summary_en: Undocumented and other students who finished high school or a GED in New York can get state college aid like TAP and Excelsior. Apply once, any time.

name: Students in Temporary Housing Transportation (McKinney-Vento)
who_can_use: Students in temporary housing under the McKinney-Vento Act: living doubled up with friends or relatives because they cannot find or afford housing; in a shelter or transitional shelter; a hotel/motel; a car, bus or train; a park or public place; or an abandoned building. Includes unaccompanied youth. Eligible for free transportation while homeless, through the end of the school year in which they become permanently housed, and for an additional year if entering the final grade in their school. Parents/guardians of students in temporary housing in 3-K to grade 12 who do not receive busing can get an OMNY card to accompany their child.
bring: The Housing Questionnaire (from your school). Students in temporary housing are not required to submit documentation (including address, proof of date of birth, and immunization records) to enroll in school.
how_to_apply: Complete the Housing Questionnaire and send it to your school. Contact your child's school to request an STH OMNY card; schools submit a Transportation Exception Form to request busing for preschool through grade 6. Help: the school's Students in Temporary Housing Liaison, your district's STH Regional Manager, or the NYS-TEACHS hotline 800-388-2014.
summary_es: Estudiantes en vivienda temporal reciben transporte gratis a la escuela en autobús escolar o tarjeta OMNY. Padres de niños de 3-K a 12.º grado sin autobús también reciben OMNY.
summary_en: Students in temporary housing ride free to school by school bus or student OMNY card. Parents of 3-K to 12th graders without busing can get OMNY too.

name: NYC Schools Account (NYCSA)
who_can_use: Parents and guardians of NYC public school students. Starting later in the 2026-2027 school year, all parents identified in NYCPS systems as the child's parent/guardian can open an account, regardless of custodial status.
bring: If you have no creation code: a valid photo ID (like your passport, driver's license, or IDNYC) and your child's nine-digit student ID number, found on your child's report card.
how_to_apply: Sign up online at https://www.schoolsaccount.nyc/ and add your students with the creation code from your school. If you do not have a creation code, register in person at your child's school or by teleconference, where the school verifies identity by voice or sight.
summary_es: Un solo acceso para ver calificaciones y exámenes de su hijo, actualizar contactos de emergencia, obtener formularios escolares y reportar acoso escolar.
summary_en: One login to see your child's grades and test scores, update emergency contacts, get school forms, and report bullying.

name: Tandas (rotating savings groups) explained
who_can_use: Informal groups. The NYC Department of Consumer Affairs study describes tandas as a common savings tool among Mexican immigrants in New York City, ranging from about 10 family members and close friends to a 50-person group run by an organizer.
summary_es: Una tanda es un grupo informal de ahorro: cada miembro aporta a un fondo común y lo recibe por turno. Sin intereses, pero puede ser riesgosa.
summary_en: A tanda is an informal savings group: members pay into a shared fund and each receives it in turn. No interest, but informal savings can be risky.

name: Lending Circles (credit-building zero-interest loans)
how_to_apply: Fill out an online application at https://www.missionassetfund.org/lending-circles/ and take the online financial education courses, then join a group, decide loan amount and order, and sign loan documents. Local nonprofit providers are listed at https://www.missionassetfund.org/lc-partner-directory/ (New York City: Harlem Congregations for Community Improvement, 212-281-4887).
summary_es: Préstamos sin interés de $300 a $2,400 en grupos de 6 a 12 personas. Los pagos se reportan a las tres agencias de crédito principales para crear historial.
summary_en: Zero-interest loans of $300 to $2,400 shared by groups of 6 to 12 people. Payments are reported to all three major credit bureaus to build credit.

name: Open a bank or credit union account with IDNYC
who_can_use: IDNYC cardholders. The City lists banks and credit unions that accept IDNYC as a primary form of ID to open an account (for example Amalgamated Bank, Carver Federal Savings Bank and East West Bank). The City says the list is provided as a convenience and is not an endorsement. Credit unions have additional membership requirements.
status_note: Depending on the bank, a Social Security number or ITIN may be required. If you have questions about how this applies to you, talk with a free legal provider before applying.
bring: Your IDNYC card. Depending on the institution, you may also need proof of address, a Social Security number or Individual Taxpayer Identification Number (ITIN), or a small initial deposit.
how_to_apply: Choose an institution from the City's list (https://www.nyc.gov/site/idnyc/benefits/banks-and-credit-unions.page) and call the branch before going. Free one-on-one help is available at NYC Financial Empowerment Centers, in English or Spanish.
summary_es: Algunos bancos y cooperativas de crédito de NYC aceptan la IDNYC como identificación principal para abrir una cuenta. Pueden pedir comprobante de domicilio, SSN o ITIN.
summary_en: Some NYC banks and credit unions accept IDNYC as primary ID to open an account. They may also ask for proof of address, SSN or ITIN.
